To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the torques that a stick insect produces to solve the task to distribute its body weight are not determined by the torques size, the number of swinging legs, the number of legs that will swing, the stepping configuration or the leg type, but by the joint type and whether a leg is going to start a swing movement.
the stick insect controls its system of 18 redundant joints by means of a set of rules that are applied to each joint individually, but that are dependent on the state of the system.
the stick insect controls the transition from standing into walking by changing the torques produced by its joints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how the nervous system solves the task of controlling a system with redundant degree of freedom.
the control of the stick insect's leg joints during the transition from standing on six legs to walking on six legs, and with the transition from standing with six legs to walking with six legs.
the question of how the stick insect controls its posture and how it chooses a solution from the abundance of possibilities to distribute its body weight onto the legs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nervous system of the stick insect uses a simple rule to initiate a first swing movement.
the transition from standing posture to walking is not a simple process.
the transition from standing posture to walking is a result of an interplay of torques that develop at different joint levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nervous system is able to produce a solution for the task of distributing the body weight onto the legs by a simple and robust control scheme.

the control system of stick insects is able to solve the redundancy of the system in such a way that the body is always well supported by the legs and the torques are always well distributed among the joints.
a stick insect controls the torques of its legs to maintain its posture and to produce swing movements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the control strategy is based on the joint type and not on the leg number, leg type or leg position in the stepping cycle.
the control of a system with redundant joints and degrees of freedom is not as simple as it might seem at first glance.
the stick insect uses a simple rule to distribute body weight onto its legs, which is based on the number of lifted off legs.
